FEATURE GUIDE

Codex usage

See your remaining weekly Codex allowance as text or a clean icon.

This Mac update · Mac

These features ship in Mac 1.5.20 build36. Windows 1.5.13 has a separate feature set; download buttons provide each platform’s public release.

OverviewHow to useExampleSupport & limitsRelated features

Overview

Codex 72% is an example of the weekly allowance remaining for a ChatGPT account. It is not a token count, request count or API cost. Click the usage row in the menu panel to open its settings.

How to use

  1. Turn on Show usage in Settings → General. It is off by default; enabling it also installs and enables the AI usage plugin.
  2. Open Usage settings or Installed plugins → AI usage below the sidebar divider. Plugin management also links to the same settings.
  3. Check the always-visible Codex connection section at the bottom. It reuses your Codex login; select an executable or choose Sign in with ChatGPT if needed.
  4. Choose Codex + % · icon + % · % only and check the center preview. Select a refresh interval and optional low-allowance notification.

Example

SettingDisplay or default
Menu barCodex + % by default; a background-free monochrome Codex symbol + % or % only are optional.
RefreshChoose 1, 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes; default 5 minutes. Manual refresh is also available.
DetailsWeekly remaining allowance, reset time, last successful refresh and observed hourly consumption.
Low-allowance alertOff by default, with a 20% remaining threshold.

Switching from text to the icon keeps the same weekly reading. The icon adapts to light and dark appearances and does not require the Codex GUI app.

Support & limits

A Codex CLI ChatGPT account is required. API-key login has no ChatGPT weekly allowance. Signing in to another account also changes the Codex CLI account.

A failed refresh labels the previous reading as stale. Hourly consumption needs two observations at least a minute apart; insufficient data shows —. The app does not assume a reset means 100% remaining.

Turning usage off stops requests, pending login and the display, while preserving settings and recent observations. Codex manages authentication; reading usage does not run model inference.
